item.title: Nintendo Shares Ocarina Of Time Switch 2 Design Sketches

description.p: Ink's awakening.The latest Ask the Developer interviews are positively packed with interesting tidbits about the making of Ocarina of Time on Switch 2. One such story is all about the game's reimagined visuals, which Nintendo was even kind enough to share some initial sketches of.According to Art Director Aya Shida, the team was consciously fighting a battle between making the game more realistic with the improved power of the Switch 2, and retaining the spirit of the original — a somewhat dark world, filled with weird characters. She therefore relied on phrases like “a puppet-show feel” and “the analogue feel of practical effects films” during development to reflect the goal: "both create a convincing sense that the characters truly exist within their respective fantasy worlds".Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Nintendo Wanted To Remake Ocarina Of Time To "Trigger New Insights" For Future Titles

description.p: Out with the old, in with the Aonuma."Hang on, why is Nintendo remaking Ocarina of Time again?" It's a natural question that might have occurred to you in the last few months, and in the latest Ask the Developer interview, Series Producer Eiji Aonuma had the answer.Part of the reason for returning to the title, it turns out, was to try to "trigger new insights" from the developers that may feed into future Zelda games. "Many of the team members who work alongside me on Legend of Zelda games today have only experienced developing the more recent titles," Aonuma-san says. "That led me to wonder, 'Do they truly understand just how significant The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time was to the series as a whole?'"Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Switch 2 Development Team Has Been Revealed

description.p: Inside job.Nintendo has just released the first two parts of a new Ask the Developer series all about The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2. item.title: Google's Ocarina Of Time Easter Egg Will Transport You Back To The Internet Of Old

description.p: Links to the past.We love it when Google pulls out a little gaming Easter Egg. We had the inkable search engine screen for Splatoon 3, the various Pokémon collaborations, and even a Katamari crossover. But now, Google has delivered the most nostalgic one of them all.If you Google 'Ocarina of Time', you'll now be met with a small Master Sword icon in the bottom right corner. Clicking on said icon pushes the sword back into its pedestal and transports the search engine into the past with it.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: The Pokémon Company Is Counting Down To A Mysterious Date On Social Media

description.p: But what's it for?The Pokémon Company is no stranger to a little over-hyping every now and then, but its latest bit of marketing has us seriously thinking that there is a big announcement in the pipeline.You see, TPC is counting down to... something. As brought to our attention by Serebii's Joe Merrick, the company has been sharing images on social media of its 30th anniversary icons, with a number underneath. Interestingly, these numbers decrease by the number of hours that have passed between each post — 1,025 on 18th October, 843 on 26th, 676 today.Read the full article on nintendolife.com
